newsitem.title: USA: Shuttle crew board shuttle for mission to Mir.
newsitem.headline: Shuttle crew board shuttle for mission to Mir.

text.p: A seven-member, multi-nation crew boarded the space shuttle Atlantis on Thursday for blastoff on a supply run to the Russian Mir space station.
The $2 billion reusable spaceship was set to make a predawn launch from Florida's Kennedy Space Centre at 4:08 a.m. EDT (0808 GMT) on Thursday at the beginning of a short seven-minute launch window.
Skies were clear over the launch site in the hours before the planned liftoff and forecasters were predicting favourable weather.
"Conditions look good for getting off the ground," shuttle weather officer Ed Priselac said.
Launch pad workers loaded the shuttle with super-cold rocket fuel as planned on Wednesday evening after overcoming two minor technical problems that arose since the countdown began on Monday.
Atlantis was to dock with the Russian orbiting space outpost on Friday night to pick up one NASA astronaut and drop off another. It will be the sixth time the U.S. shuttle has linked up with Mir.
The shuttle crew, wearing flame-orange pressure suits, said a last goodbye to friends and relatives and bounded out of their quarters smiling, waving and blowing kisses to a small, cheering crowd.
After a short bus ride to the brilliantly lit launch pad, they began taking their seats aboard Atlantis at about 1 a.m. EDT (0500 GMT).

The crew, which includes a woman pilot, a Russian woman, a Frenchman, natives of Britain and Peru, and an astronaut of Chinese descent, is one of the most diverse selected by NASA for a space shuttle mission.

The mission will be led by a two-time shuttle flier, Charlie Precourt. Joining him on the flight deck is Eileen Collins, who became NASA's first woman shuttle pilot in February 1995 on the first shuttle mission to fly close to Mir.

Also on board shuttle Discovery during that mission was Michael Foale, the British-born astronaut, Atlantis is ferrying to Mir. And Elena Kondakova, the cosmonaut who is guest astronaut on Atlantis' mission, was a Mir crew member during that mid-space rendezvous.
Rounding out the crew are mission specialists Jean-Francois Clervoy, a French astronaut from European Space Agency; Edward Lu, an astrophysicist; and Carlos Noriega, who was born in Lima, Peru.
The shuttle's planned blastoff will begin a two-day chase through space to catch up with Mir, where U.S. astronaut Jerry Linenger is nearing the end of a four-month tour of duty.
He will be relieved by Foale, who is to live and work on Mir until mid-September. He will be the fifth NASA astronaut to stay on the Russian station.
Foale was trained to help his cosmonaut crewmates maintain the 11-year-old space station, which had suffered numerous mechanical breakdowns, one of which led to a serious fire in February.
Atlantis is carrying 4,000 lbs (1,814 kg) of supplies and equipment to Mir, including a replacement oxygen generator and repair gear to patch up a leaky cooling system.
